newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia Oct palm oil output up 1.8 pct - Ivan Wong.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia Oct palm oil output up 1.8 pct - Ivan Wong.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in October was estimated to have risen 1.8 percent to 880,000 tonnes over September, private crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Thursday.
This compared with his earlier projection of a three percent fall to 840,000 tonnes.

Wong estimated end-October palm oil stocks at 965,000 tonnes, unchanged from his earlier forecast, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 894,030 tonnes at end-September.
Wong said palm oil exports in October were estimated at 710,000 tonnes, a record high, against an estimated 680,000 tonnes shipped in September. He earlier forecast October exports at 670,000 tonnes.

"Production in Peninsular Malaysia rose around one percent or 6,000 tonnes to an estimated 653,000 tonnes. The seasonal increase in East Malaysia also moderated to around five percent from 24.4 percent in September and 37.3 percent in August," Wong said in his latest report.
He said the oil extraction rate remained good, aided in part by favourable weather conditions in most crop areas.
In October, reduced exports to India were more than offset by increased shipments to countries in the European Union, Pakistan and China, Wong said.
"The better than expected export performance in October was attributed to some extent by shortfalls in export availabilities from Indonesia," he said.
Wong said the entire build-up in palm oil stocks was in the form of crude palm oil which rose to an estimated 610,000 tonnes from around 525,000 tonnes at end-September.
